items.bron: Britannica Kids, 'matter' (kids.britannica.com/kids/article/matter/353444): 'anything that takes up space is called matter'. The fuller scientific definition adds mass (NRC Science 101, AMNH ology); the lesson's wording is the incomplete-but-true school form, not a false one.

items.bewering: Alle materie bestaan uit baie klein deeltjies, of dit 'n vaste stof, 'n vloeistof of 'n gas is.
items.bron: Victoria Department of Education, science continuum 'Movement of particles' (education.vic.gov.au); EBSCO Research Starters 'Kinetic theory'. Universal claim of the particle model; holds for all three states.

items.bewering: Hulle is te klein om met die oog of met 'n vergrootglas te sien.
items.bron: Water molecule about 0.28 nm across, far below the ~200 nm diffraction limit of even a light microscope (Physics Forums Insights 'Can we see an atom?'; scaleofuniverse.com water molecule). A magnifying glass resolves far less than a microscope.

items.bewering: In al drie toestande beweeg die deeltjies altyd.
items.bron: Victoria Department of Education, 'Movement of particles': 'Particles in all states of matter are in constant motion' and in solids they 'vibrate about fixed positions; even at very low temperatures'.

items.bewering: Ys smelt tot water en kookwater word waterdamp. Laat daardie damp teen 'n koue deksel afkoel en dit word weer druppels water.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Condensation': water vapour meeting a cooler surface loses energy and becomes liquid droplets; condensation is the reverse of evaporation.

items.bewering: Ys, water en waterdamp bestaan dus uit dieselfde waterdeeltjies.
items.bron: Max-Planck-Gesellschaft, 'The smallest ice crystals in the world' (ice is water molecules in a hexagonal lattice); Wikipedia 'Evaporation' / LibreTexts evaporation (water molecules leave the liquid as vapour). State changes are physical; the molecules are the same.

items.bewering: Die deeltjies self word nie groter of kleiner wanneer die water van toestand verander nie.
items.bron: NSW Department of Education, 'Particle Model of Matter - Expansion and contraction': the belief that particles themselves expand is a named misconception; particle size and mass stay the same. Victoria DoE 'Movement of particles' lists particles that 'shrink' as a student misconception.

items.bewering: 'n Enkele deeltjie is ook nie nat of koud of hard soos die stof self nie.
items.bron: RSC Education, 'Students' ideas about the particulate nature of matter' (Beyond appearances); Victoria DoE 'Movement of particles': students confuse 'the properties of the particles with the macroscopic nature of the materials that they make up'.

items.bewering: Daar kom geen deeltjies by nie en geen deeltjie verdwyn nie.
items.bron: Same sources as the state-change items (National Geographic Education 'Condensation'; LibreTexts evaporation): a change of state rearranges the same particles; none are created or destroyed. Read in context (the water's own particles), it is correct; particles that evaporate leave the container but do not disappear, which the sentence does not deny.

items.bewering: Net drie dinge verander: hoe naby die deeltjies aan mekaar is, of hulle vaste plekke het en hoe hulle beweeg.
items.bron: Victoria DoE 'Movement of particles'; CK-12 'Describe the arrangement and the motion of particles in solid, liquid and gas'. Spacing, fixed position and motion are the variables of the particle model. Checked for the ice-water trap: liquid water's molecules are slightly closer than in ice, and the sentence only says spacing changes, not in which direction, so it holds.

items.bewering: In 'n vaste stof is die deeltjies baie naby aan mekaar met net klein ruimtes tussen hulle. Elke deeltjie bly op sy eie vaste plek. Dit staan nie stil nie maar vibreer heeltyd daar.
items.bron: Victoria DoE 'Movement of particles': particles in solids 'vibrate about fixed positions; even at very low temperatures'; EBSCO Research Starters 'Kinetic theory'.

items.bewering: In sout en metale sit die deeltjies styf gepak in 'n netjiese patroon.
items.bron: LibreTexts 'Lattices and unit cells of salt' / 'Rock salt (NaCl)': ions alternate in a regular repeating cubic lattice. Open University OpenLearn 'What is a metal? 2 Arrangement of atoms in metals': metal atoms closely packed in a repeating pattern.

items.bewering: In ys sit die deeltjies ook in 'n netjiese patroon.
items.bron: American Meteorological Society Glossary 'ice crystal' (hexagonal lattice); Max-Planck-Gesellschaft 'The smallest ice crystals in the world'. Correctly not described as 'styf gepak' (ice's lattice is open).

items.bewering: Glas se deeltjies het ook vaste plekke maar nie so 'n netjiese patroon nie.
items.bron: Britannica 'Amorphous solid - atomic-scale structure' and 'Short-range order': glass lacks long-range order; below the glass transition the atoms are frozen into fixed positions. Scientific American 'Fact or fiction: glass is a (supercooled) liquid' confirms glass is a solid.

items.bewering: Vaste plekke geld dus vir elke vaste stof.
items.bron: Victoria DoE 'Movement of particles' (solids vibrate about fixed positions); Britannica 'Amorphous solid' (fixed positions hold for non-crystalline solids too). Universal claim; holds at the particle-model level taught here.

items.bewering: In 'n vloeistof is die deeltjies ook baie naby aan mekaar met net klein ruimtes tussen hulle. Tog het geeneen 'n vaste plek nie en hulle sit ook nie in 'n patroon nie. Hulle beweeg heeltyd en gly verby mekaar.
items.bron: Victoria DoE 'Movement of particles': liquid particles are 'quite close together' and 'have no fixed positions'; CK-12 Flexi: liquid particles slide past each other with a disordered arrangement.

items.bewering: In 'n gas is die deeltjies ver uitmekaar met groot ruimtes tussen hulle.
items.bron: CK-12 'Compressibility - kinetic molecular theory'; EBSCO Research Starters 'Kinetic theory'. At room conditions the average spacing is about ten molecular diameters.

items.bewering: Daardie ruimtes is heeltemal leeg. Lug bestaan uit gasse, en selfs tussen lug se deeltjies is geen lug nie.
items.bron: RSC Education, 'Students' ideas about the particulate nature of matter' (Novick and Nussbaum): the scientific model has empty space between gas particles; 'air' or other matter between them is a documented misconception. NASA Glenn 'Properties of air': air is a mixture of gases (78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, traces of others).

items.bewering: Die deeltjies beweeg vrylik in alle rigtings en gaan ver voordat hulle teen mekaar of die wande van hulle houer bots.
items.bron: Victoria DoE: gas particles 'move rapidly in all directions, frequently colliding with each other and the side of the container'. Boston University physics 'Mean free path' / schoolphysics.co.uk: mean free path in air at room conditions ~68 nm, roughly 180-200 molecular diameters, so 'ver' is right relative to particle size.

items.bewering: Vaste stof: die deeltjies is baie naby aan mekaar. Elkeen vibreer op sy eie vaste plek. / Vloeistof: die deeltjies is ook baie naby aan mekaar. Sonder vaste plekke gly hulle verby mekaar. / Gas: die deeltjies is ver uitmekaar. Sonder vaste plekke beweeg hulle vrylik in alle rigtings.
items.bron: Victoria DoE 'Movement of particles'; CK-12 Flexi on arrangement and motion. Summary items match the study blocks and the sources.

items.bewering: 'n Tekening van die drie wys dieselfde getal ewe groot deeltjies. Net hulle rangskikking verskil.
items.bron: NSW DoE 'Particle Model of Matter' (particle size unchanged between states) and RSC Education particle-diagram misconceptions. As a statement of how a correct diagram of one substance in three states is drawn, it is sound: same particles, same size, only arrangement shown. Motion also differs, but a still drawing shows arrangement only, so 'net hulle rangskikking' is accurate for the drawing.

items.bewering: 'n Vaste stof hou sy vorm omdat elke deeltjie op sy plek bly. 'n Vloeistof vloei en neem sy houer se vorm aan omdat sy deeltjies verby mekaar gly. 'n Gas versprei en vul sy houer omdat sy deeltjies vrylik oral heen beweeg.
items.bron: CK-12 Flexi: liquid particles slide past each other, which allows liquids to flow and adapt to the container's shape; EBSCO 'Kinetic theory'; Victoria DoE 'Movement of particles'.

items.bewering: Jy kan die lug in 'n ballon saamdruk omdat daar groot leë ruimtes tussen die deeltjies is.
items.bron: CK-12 'Compressibility - kinetic molecular theory': gases compress because of the large empty space between particles, while solids and liquids have little to reduce.

items.bewering: Hitte laat deeltjies meer beweeg. Verhit ys en die deeltjies vibreer al hoe sterker. Later breek hulle van hulle vaste plekke los en begin verby mekaar gly. Dan smelt die ys.
items.bron: LibreTexts 'Melting' (CK-12 Introductory Chemistry 13.11) and Doc Brown's Chemistry kinetic particle model of melting: heating increases vibration; at the melting point particles break free of fixed positions and slide past one another. Nothing in the block implies vibration keeps rising during melting.

items.bewering: In 'n vloeistof kan deeltjies wat vinnig genoeg beweeg by die oppervlak ontsnap en 'n gas word. Hoe warmer die vloeistof is, hoe meer deeltjies ontsnap en hoe vinniger verdamp dit.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Evaporation'; LibreTexts 'Evaporation' (CK-12 Introductory Chemistry 13.8); Energy Education (University of Calgary) 'Evaporation': molecules with enough kinetic energy escape the surface, and a higher temperature gives a larger fraction such molecules and faster evaporation.

items.bewering: Afkoel werk andersom.
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'Condensation' (the reverse of evaporation, as particles lose energy); LibreTexts 'Melting' (freezing is the reverse of melting).

items.bron: Victoria DoE 'Movement of particles'; Physics Forums Insights 'Can we see an atom?' (below the resolution even of light microscopes). Read on its own, the entry is true.

items.bron: Victoria DoE 'Movement of particles'; EBSCO 'Kinetic theory'. Read on its own, the entry is true.

items.bron: CK-12 Flexi on arrangement and motion of particles; Victoria DoE 'Movement of particles'.

items.bron: Wiktionary 'vibrate' ('to shake with small, rapid movements to and fro'); Wordnik ('to move back and forth or to and fro, especially rhythmically and rapidly').

opsomming: Every claim in the lesson checks out against sources, including the careful ones: ice is left out of the 'tightly packed' group, glass is a solid with no neat pattern, and the space between gas particles is empty. The lesson has no superlatives such as 'first' or 'largest' and no analogies; its absolute claims ('all matter', 'always moving', 'completely empty', 'every solid') are recorded as superlative items and all hold.
